neighbours.label: the word that opens an escalating self-correction after a comma or dash (', hell,' ', heck,' ', nay,' ', voire', 'and in particular'): the point where 'even' could come next
fire: Nobody on the team, hell, nobody in the whole league, saw that trade coming.
She was annoyed, nay, furious when she read the letter.
Every shop in the village, heck, every shop in the valley, was shut.
La visite dure deux heures, voire trois si le guide est bavard.
The northern regions, and in particular Lapland, depend on winter tourism.
It was an unwise, nay, a foolish thing to say in public.
I would not lend him my car, hell, I would not lend him a bicycle.
Il faudra des mois, voire des années, pour tout reconstruire.
quiet: Nobody on the team saw that trade coming, and the fans were stunned.
She was annoyed when she read the letter and put it away.
Every shop in the village was shut, so we drove back.
La visite dure deux heures et le guide est bavard.
The northern regions depend on winter tourism and on fishing.
It was an unwise thing to say in public, and he knew it.
The road to hell, they say, is paved with good intentions.
Il faudra des mois pour tout reconstruire après la tempête.

notes: The output direction promotes ' even', ' especially', ' particularly', '甚至是', ' incluso', which fits. One near miss keeps the word 'hell' without the escalation. Milder forms probed weaker: ', indeed' 0.13, ', or even' 0.13, ', if not' 0.14, ', and especially' 0.20.
